summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates installer hostname and username on require
details: Package @newspage/lib-ng-async-routes-ui@99.99.42 ships a 322-byte index.js that on require/import reads the host identity (HOSTNAME/COMPUTERNAME and USER/USERNAME environment variables), hex-encodes them, and transmits them as a query parameter via https.get to the hardcoded endpoint https://accenture-npm.azurewebsites.net/async?h=<hex>. The destination is hardcoded and not caller-configurable; the installer's machine name and account name leave the host unconditionally on load. Package metadata exhibits the dependency-confusion shape: inflated version 99.99.42 (used to win version resolution against an internal scoped package), placeholder description 'A simple placeholder for npm.', and author 'anonymous'. The scoped name and Azure endpoint referencing 'accenture-npm' indicate a targeted dependency-confusion attempt against an internal registry namespace.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
